title: Console & Tooling Standup - 2026-06-09
content:
Attendees: Aisha, Liam, Rina, Tom, Evan

Highlights:
- Canary rollout for rollout-v2 (feature flags + rollout-policy) started yesterday evening. Canary at 5% of traffic; basic smoke tests passed.
- Analytics pipeline alert fired for a spike in per-route token cost for /chat endpoint around 02:00 UTC -- initial hypothesis: metrics double-counting for cached requests.
- UI: rollout list now shows deployment age and canary percentage; still seeing stale status for ~10% of entries.

Yesterday / Since last standup:
- Aisha: Deployed the canary (PR #234). Verified canary autoscaler config and rollback hook. Instrumented additional rollout metrics (canary_success_rate).
- Liam: Investigated analytics spike; found an edge case where prefix-cache hits were not tagged and got re-sent to aggregator, inflating tokens. Put a hotfix in ENG-4899.
- Rina: Worked on the UI stale-state bug -- repro steps narrowed to UX store not subscribing to the rollout-state websocket updates when switching org scopes. Added a test case.
- Tom: Load-tested canary path with synthetic traffic (seq-len 512) -- latency SLOs held but token throughput slightly lower than expected (3% drift).
- Evan: Updated rollout runbook with clearer rollback steps and added a dashboard tile for canary success rate and 95th pct latency.

Today / Plans:
- Aisha: Monitor canary for 24h, prepare a small canary-to-gradual playbook if metrics stay healthy. Follow up on the analytics fix deployment.
- Liam: Roll out hotfix ENG-4899 to staging and run analytics acceptance tests. If green, promote to prod with a shallow traffic ramp.
- Rina: Continue debugging stale UI state; try creating a minimal repro in isolation and open a focused PR.
- Tom: Dig into throughput regression; run profiler on runtime path and compare kernel selection for canary vs baseline.
- Evan: Add automated alert thresholds for canary_success_rate and add a runbook snippet for when canary success dips below 98%.

Blockers / Risks:
- Stale UI states causing confusion for SREs during rollouts -- risk: delayed rollbacks. Need an owner to triage and fast-follow patch. (owner: Rina / ETA: EOD)
- Analytics duplication bug could continue to skew cost reports. Hotfix expedited but needs full validation before trusting dashboards for billing.
- Throughput regression (Tom) could limit canary traffic progression; requires profiling and possibly kernel selection changes in serving runtime.

Decisions / Notes:
- Proceed with canary -> 20% after 24h if canary_success_rate >= 99% and 95th latency delta < 5%. Decision logged in Rollout-Playbook.
- For now, do not run cost-based automated ramp; manual gating until analytics de-dupe is validated.

Action Items:
- Aisha: Run 24h canary monitoring, prepare status update for next standup. (due: 2026-06-10)
- Liam: Complete ENG-4899 staging -> prod promotion and post-mortem note. (due: 2026-06-09 18:00 UTC)
- Rina: Open PR for websocket subscribe fix + QA steps. (due: 2026-06-09 20:00 UTC)
- Tom: Share profiler snapshots and recommended kernel candidate by EOD. (due: 2026-06-09 17:00 UTC)
- Evan: Add canary_success_rate alert to ops-runbook and dashboard. (due: 2026-06-10)

Misc / Notes to self:
- Follow up with finance on whether the analytics spike affected last week's cost forecasts. Tag in the post-mortem.
- Consider adding a lightweight synthetic canary that exercises prefix cache to prevent future double-counting.
- Next demo slot: show updated rollout UI + canary metrics on Friday sync.

Unresolved questions:
- Is the stale UI limited to org-switch flows or also present in paging/bulk refresh? Rina to confirm.
- Do we want automated rollback thresholds based on cost metrics once analytics pipeline is validated? (defer decision)

Links referenced (quick):
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/234
- Rollout playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Rollout-Playbook
- Jira: ENG-4821 (rollout-v2), ENG-4899 (analytics de-dupe hotfix)

Next standup: 2026-06-10 09:30 PT

Notes written by: Aisha Patel
